headline: DENR Says Indonesia Wildfire Haze Reached the Philippines as NCR Air Quality Improves
seoTitle: Indonesia Haze Reaches PH; NCR Air Improves | FMB News
seoDescription: DENR-EMB said haze linked to fires in Indonesia affected parts of the Philippines, while changing winds improved Metro Manila air quality on September 2.
deck: The haze shifted with changing winds, underscoring how transboundary smoke can quickly change local air-quality conditions.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The DENR Environmental Management Bureau said haze associated with forest and peatland fires in Indonesia had affected parts of the Philippines, including Metro Manila.
By Wednesday, air quality in Metro Manila had improved as wind direction shifted the haze away from Luzon toward parts of the Visayas and Mindanao.

sections.heading: Health context
paragraphs: Air-quality conditions varied by monitoring station and time. Sensitive groups were advised to reduce prolonged outdoor exposure when local readings reached unhealthy levels.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Transboundary haze can change rapidly with wind direction, so a clear skyline in one period does not necessarily mean the regional smoke episode has ended.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should use official air-quality monitoring and public-health advisories for current conditions rather than rely on visibility alone.
